newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seeks Japanese assurance over Asia push.
newsitem.headline: Australia seeks Japanese assurance over Asia push.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday sought an assurance from Japan that it backed Canberra's engagement with Asia after a media report suggested Tokyo's support was waning because of Australia's race debate.
Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said he had asked for, and received, an assurance that Japan still backed Australia's bid to win a seat at the biennial Asia-Europe leaders' summit.
The daily Australian Financial Review quoted an unnamed Japanese foreign ministry official as saying Canberra's handling of the race debate had thrown Japan's support into doubt.

Australia's position on Burma's accession to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) also caused Japan to question its strong support for Canberra's inclusion in the Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM), the newspaper reported on Wednesday.
Australia was excluded from last year's inaugural summit in Bangkok. It is counting on Japan, its closest Asian ally, to help it obtain a seat at the table in future.
"On my instructions, my department has asked what the source of this story is. Of course no-one knows," Downer told reporters in Melbourne after making a speech on Australia-Japan ties.
"We have had discussions in Tokyo with Japanese officials about this and they completely repudiate the views which have been expressed by some unnamed official...," he added.
Australia sees membership of the ASEM as an important foreign policy goal and a way of cementing its position in the region.
New membership of ASEM is due to be considered at the next summit in London next April. ASEM groups 10 Asian nations with the 15 nations of the European Union.
Japan's ambassador to Australia, Yukio Satoh, on Wednesday expressed Japan's strong support for Australia joining ASEM.

"On Prime Minister (Ryutaro) Hashimoto's instructions, I have already conveyed to Prime Minister (John) Howard his message that Australia can continue to count on Japan's strong and unequivocal support...," Satoh said.
Downer denied the race debate, sparked by far-right legislator Pauline Hanson last year, was hindering Canberra's efforts to secure membership of ASEM.
Hanson has said she believes Australia is in danger of being "swamped" by Asians and wants immigration curtailed.

Earlier on Wednesday, Downer released a foreign ministry report which urged Australian business to exploit Japanese economic deregulation and new trade opportunities in Japan, seen as a tough market to crack but still Asia's largest economy.

Japan has been Australia's biggest trade partner since the 1960s, taking vast shipments of commodities like coal and iron ore. But Australia's share of the Japanese market is slipping as raw materials account for less of Japan's imports.
